seo.metaTitle: Date Stamp PNG - Free Browser Tool With a Format String
seo.metaDescription: Write the current date and time onto a picture with a YYYY-MM-DD format string, then style it like any caption. Free, it runs in your browser and nothing is uploaded.
seo.longDescription: Date stamp writes the current date and time onto an image, so a photo, a screenshot or a scan carries visible proof of when it was made. Instead of typing a caption by hand you type a short format string and the tokens are substituted — YYYY for the year, MM and DD for the month and day, hh, mm and ss for hours, minutes and seconds, read from the clock of your device in local time. Everything else you type is kept as it is, so the separators are yours to choose. The stamp is styled like any other caption: font, size, weight, color, one of nine positions, a margin and an optional backing plate. The lettering is drawn by the browser on your device, so the picture is never uploaded.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Tokens YYYY, MM, DD, hh, mm, ss; every other character is kept as you type it.
The date is read from your device clock in local time — a visible label, not file metadata.
Nine positions on a 3x3 grid, margin, and an optional backing plate for contrast.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Edit the Date format field - YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss fills year, month, day, hours, minutes and seconds.
Set the text style, then choose one of nine positions and adjust the margin from the edge.
Turn the plate on or off for contrast, then download the stamped image.

faq.a: YYYY, MM, DD, hh, mm and ss, written in exactly that case. Every other character is left alone, so the default YYYY-MM-DD works and DD.MM.YYYY or YYYY/MM/DD hh:mm are just as easy to type.

faq.q: Is the date read from the file?
faq.a: No. It reads the clock of the device at the moment the stamp is drawn, in local time. This is a visible label on the pixels, not metadata written inside the file.

A sans-serif, a serif and a monospace family, all rendered by the browser from the fonts installed on your device. That is also why a stamp can look slightly different on another machine, while the picture itself looks identical everywhere.
This tool writes the current date and time from the format string. To write any text you type yourself - a name, a caption, a label - use the add text tool on this site instead.
